# Genesis Apocryphon Column 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 21 | **Condition:** Well preserved; substantially legible

---

**21:1** an-afflicting-spirit upon-him and-upon all the-men of-his-household, an-evil-spirit.

**21:2** And-it-afflicted-him and-all the-men of-his-house, and-he-could-not approach-her

**21:3** nor-did-he-know-her, though-she-was with-him for-two-years.

**21:4** And-at the-end of-two-years the-plagues and-the-afflictions grew-great

**21:5** and-severe upon-him and-upon all the-men of-his-house.

**21:6** And-he-sent for-all the-wise-men of-Egypt and-all the-magicians

**21:7** and-all the-healers of-Egypt, if-perhaps they-could-heal-him

**21:8** and-the-men of-his-house from-this-plague.

**21:9** But none of-the-healers and-the-magicians and-all the-wise-men

**21:10** could-stand to-heal-him, for-the-spirit afflicted-them-all

**21:11** and-they-fled from-before-him.

**21:12** Then Harkenosh came to-me and-asked-me to-come

**21:13** and-to-pray for-the-king and-to-lay my-hands upon-him

**21:14** that-he-might-live, for-he-had-seen-me in-a-dream.

**21:15** But Lot said to-him: Abram my-uncle cannot-pray for-the-king

**21:16** while Sarai his-wife is with-the-king. Go and-tell the-king

**21:17** to-send-away the-wife of-Abram to-her-husband, and-he-will-pray for-him

**21:18** and-he-shall-live.

**21:19** And-when Harkenosh heard the-words of-Lot, he-went and-said to-the-king:

**21:20** All-these-plagues and-these-afflictions with-which my-lord the-king

**21:21** is-afflicted and-stricken are-because-of Sarai the-wife of-Abram.

**21:22** Restore Sarai to-Abram her-husband, and-this-plague

**21:23** and-the-spirit of-pestilence shall-depart from-you.

**21:24** And-the-king called Abram and-said to-him: What have-you-done to-me

**21:25** regarding Sarai? You-told-me, She is my-sister, but-she is your-wife!

**21:26** I-took-her to-be my-wife. Behold-her — your-wife — take-her and-go

**21:27** from-all the-land of-Egypt. And-now pray for-me and-for my-house

**21:28** that-this-evil-spirit may-be-rebuked from-us.

**21:29** And-I-prayed for-him [...] and-I-laid my-hands upon-his-head.

**21:30** And-the-plague departed from-him and-the-evil-spirit was-rebuked,

**21:31** and-he-lived.

**21:32** And-the-king rose and-said to-me [...] and-the-king swore to-me an-oath

**21:33** that-he-had-not touched-her. And-Sarai was-brought to-me.

**21:34** And-the-king gave-her silver and-gold and-much fine-linen and-purple.

---

*EMET notes: Column 21 is well preserved and contains the dramatic climax of the Egypt episode. The plague narrative (21:1-11) expands Genesis 12:17 into a two-year ordeal. Lot's role as intermediary (21:15-18) is unique to the Apocryphon. The healing through laying on of hands (21:29) presents Abraham as a prophetic healer, a significant theological development. "Spirit of pestilence" (rucha mare'ita) is the same compound from 20:34. Construct chains preserved with hyphens.*
